text:
pat: Urgent: BetaBank POC keeps triggering auth retries behind their corp proxy + SSO (IdP). After a token refresh, their client immediately retries same request and we end up with a retry storm -> 429s and demo failing. Anyone seen SSO + proxy lead to repeated 401/429 loops?

zara-sales: Demo tomorrow, customer very unhappy. CC @oliver-eng @nina-sdks @kevin-auth. They said they use our node SDK and a short-lived OAuth token via their IdP refresh flow.

oliver-eng: Can you paste sequence of events/logs? Is the SDK doing automatic retries on 401?

pat: Snippet from logs: 
```
2026-03-21T09:02:01Z INFO  client: request POST /v1/chat -> 401
2026-03-21T09:02:01Z INFO  auth: refresh token start
2026-03-21T09:02:01Z INFO  client: retrying request #1
2026-03-21T09:02:01Z WARN  proxy: CONNECT returned 407 (Proxy Auth Required)
2026-03-21T09:02:02Z INFO  auth: refresh token success
2026-03-21T09:02:02Z INFO  client: retrying request #2
2026-03-21T09:02:02Z ERROR rate-limiter: rejected (burst) -> 429
```
They show many CONNECT 407s from their proxy during the same timeframe and a flurry of client retries while the IdP refresh is in-flight.

nina-sdks: The SDK's default retry behavior will eagerly retry on 401/5xx with no jitter if the app config asks for automatic retries. If the auth refresh is happening asynchronously, multiple concurrent requests can all detect 401 and trigger parallel refresh+retry. Combined with a proxy that sometimes demands reauth (407) you can get amplified retries hitting our ingest/rate-limiter.

kevin-auth: On the IdP side they said refresh tokens are single-use for short windows. If multiple clients attempt refresh simultaneously, some will fail and then retry again, making the loop worse. Also the proxy 407 means the handshake isn't completing for some retries so those retries leave sockets half-open.

pat: Customer code uses a naive pattern: 
```
async function doChat() {
  try {
    await sdk.chat.create(...)
  } catch (err) {
    if (err.status === 401) {
      await auth.refresh();
      return sdk.chat.create(...); // immediate retry
    }
  }
}
```
They spawn multiple parallel requests that use this logic.

oliver-eng: Short-term mitigation we can ask them to apply immediately:
- Add a single-flight lock around token refresh so only one refresh runs and others wait for its result. (mutex / promise share).
- Add jittered backoff before retrying after refresh (100-500ms).
- Stop automatic eager retries in SDK config (set retries=0) while they patch client auth flow.

nina-sdks: Also recommend setting SDK option retryOn401=false (we'll add this key) and use our token-refresh helper which exposes refreshLock. Example quick change: 
```
// pseudo
if (err.status === 401) {
  await sdk.auth.refreshOnce(); // global single-flight
  await sleep(random(100,500));
  return sdk.chat.create(...);
}
```

kevin-auth: For POC we can also suggest switching the IdP to issue slightly longer-lived tokens (e.g., +30s) or allow parallel refreshes for the demo to avoid single-use collisions. They said they can do that temporarily.

pat: Anything we can change server-side to be more tolerant? We want to avoid telling customer to disable security rules.

oliver-eng: Server-side, we can temporarily relax burst rate limits for that customer tag (account-id) for 30 minutes of the demo window. Ops needs approval. That reduces 429 amplification while they patch.

monitor-bot: rate-alert: BetaBank POC hitting 429s (count=312) over 5m window.

zara-sales: Please do both: ask customer for single-flight pattern + short jitter and request ops to temporarily raise burst quota for their account during demo. I'll coordinate with the customer.

nina-sdks: We'll add a small helper function into the next patch of the SDK that provides a ready-made refreshOnce() utility that uses a promise mutex and prevents duplicate refresh calls. We can provide them a quick patch or snippet to paste. Target RC today.

pat: Ok I'm sending the snippet and asking Ops for temporary quota bump. Thanks team — will report back after the demo.
